title: Network Topology Does Not Matter: The Breakdown of Classical Consensus in LLM Populations
abstract: arXiv:2610.37699v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: As multi-agent language model networks become widely deployed, predicting their collective behavior is a critical challenge. Classical distributed consensus theory relies on network topology to predict convergence, structurally assuming that agent updates are convex combinations, population means are conserved, and weights are content-independent. In this work, we demonstrate that these foundational assumptions fail for large language models (LLMs). By deterministically extracting continuous credence from token-level probabilities across eight instruction-tuned models and 73,080 controlled exchanges, we directly measure the empirical LLM update operator. We find that LLMs systematically violate convexity by updating outside the hull of observed opinions, exhibiting active repulsion (negative weights) that fundamentally breaks row-stochastic modeling and standard bounded-confidence repairs. tldr: 本研究通过直接测量大语言模型的经验更新算子，发现LLM群体会系统性违反经典共识理论的核心假设——在观测意见凸包之外进行更新并表现出负权重主动排斥，因此网络拓扑结构无法预测其共识收敛行为。
